text.en: The lights will not turn on, the internet is gone and the tap runs dry. This is what life would be like without infrastructure. Next, follow Satish, a tomato farmer from Maharashtra: he sells his tomatoes at the mandi, rides a train home, and his money reaches his bank by phone. Roads, trains, power and networks all work together like pieces of a puzzle. This chapter is about infrastructure, the engine of development.

Infrastructure is the vast network of structures and services that keep cities and villages functioning: roads, railways, airports, ports, power, water supply, communication and more. A developed India, said Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, will be one where urban and rural areas have the same infrastructure: roads, power, water and communication. These parts are connected like pieces of a puzzle and help people and goods travel safely and on time. India has had a network of trade routes since ancient times and modern infrastructure carries it forward.
Local roads help children reach school, farmers carry crops to markets and ambulances reach hospitals. National highways and expressways, built and maintained by the central government, join cities across states. The highway from Srinagar in the north to Kanyakumari in the south is among the great links of the country. When a new highway is built near a village, people can travel faster and sell produce further away. Bridges and tunnels ease access where rivers and mountains block roads. A bridge on the Brahmaputra in Assam has replaced ferries that did not run during floods. In Meghalaya the Khasi and Jaintia tribes shape the roots of the Indian rubber tree, Ficus elastica, into living root bridges, nurtured over generations.
Indian Railways began in 1853. As the railway network expanded, trade grew, major markets developed and new settlements emerged near stations. Cargo trains carry coal, grains, textiles and electronics using 75 to 90 percent less energy than road transport. Trains and metros offer fast, reliable travel, make daily commutes easier and reduce road traffic. A railway station is also a place of economic activity, with food vendors, porters and shops.
Airports connect distant cities quickly and help deliver aid in disasters like floods and earthquakes, since planes and helicopters can reach difficult terrain such as high mountains, deserts and dense forests. Ships dock at ports, where goods are loaded and unloaded. Ports on India's long coastline are gateways for foreign trade.
Behind a simple message such as Namaste sent across India is a hidden world of cables, wireless devices, towers, satellites and data centres. E-commerce means buying and selling goods by the internet, and even small businesses can sell across the world. Jagadish Chandra Bose showed in 1895 in Calcutta that signals could pass through a wall to ring a bell and fire a remote-controlled gun. He invented the galena crystal detector, an early semiconductor device, antennas and waveguides, but rarely patented his inventions. A patent is a right granted by the government to an inventor. In the 1990s a mobile call in India could cost up to Rs 17 a minute, even for incoming calls, while today it is very cheap.
India has built major infrastructure, yet challenges remain. Taking care of public infrastructure is a collective responsibility. Report damage such as potholes and broken streetlights and do not scribble on walls or damage benches. According to Kautilya's Arthashastra the state, the gramas and the sabhas took part in building and maintaining roads and waterways, and rules and fines stopped misuse. New roads and airports must be built with care for the environment, and we can make schools eco-friendly.

problem.en: Trace Satish's tomatoes from farm to city. Which types of infrastructure are used?

text.en: Local road to the mandi.
Trucks or trains carry tomatoes to city markets.
Phones and banks send payments.

prompt.en: Why is infrastructure called the engine of development?

requiredIdeas.en: It makes trade, travel and communication faster.
It brings services such as power and water to people.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking public property belongs to nobody.

points.en: Infrastructure includes roads, rail, air, ports, power, water and communication.
It supports trade, jobs and daily life.
Railways began in 1853 and rail cargo saves energy.
Public infrastructure is our shared responsibility.
